drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > The contract price and the final price
drafts.claim: The director of Osmani International Airport, Sylhet, said on 18 April 2026 that many of the victims heard at that day's roundtable had spent BDT 10 to 15 lakh, and up to BDT 20 lakh, to go abroad.
quotes: ১০ থেকে ১৫ লাখ টাকা, এমনকি ২০ লাখ টাকা পর্যন্ত
drafts.why_new: A Sylhet-side spending range for irregular journeys, from survivors' testimony at one meeting.

drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > The numbers
drafts.claim: The general secretary of the Sylhet District Press Club said on 18 April 2026 that over the previous 10 years at least 10,000 people had died or gone missing, more than two and a half lakh had been trafficked abroad by illegal routes and at least 15,000 had been jailed in various countries (he gave no source).
quotes: গত ১০ বছরের একটি চিত্র তুলে ধরলে দেখা যায়, অন্তত ১০ হাজার মানুষ নিহত বা নিখোঁজ হয়েছেন, আড়াই লাখের বেশি মানুষ অবৈধ পথে পাচার হয়ে বিদেশে গেছেন এবং অন্তত ১৫ হাজার মানুষ পৃথিবীর বিভিন্ন দেশে বন্দী হয়েছেন
drafts.why_new: Ten-year totals from a speaker with no source given; usable only with attribution or after checking.

drafts.target_section: NEW: From the Gulf overland through Iran and Turkey to Greece
drafts.claim: Sujan Mia of Simtola village, Chhatak, Sunamganj, said on 18 April 2026 that he first went from Bangladesh to Oman for construction work, moved to Dubai after a problem with his iqama (residence permit) and then worked in Qatar, and later returned to Dubai to head for Europe, going through Oman to Iran, Turkey, Greece, North Macedonia and Serbia, working illegally to survive.
quotes: প্রথমে বাংলাদেশ থেকে ওমানে গিয়ে
আবার ওমান হয়ে ইরান, তুরস্ক, গ্রিস, নর্থ মেসিডোনিয়া ও সার্বিয়া যাই
drafts.why_new: A second, later account of the Dubai-Oman-Iran-Turkey-Greece route, supporting a section for it.

drafts.target_section: The Balkans and Eastern Europe > The path
drafts.claim: Sujan Mia said that, finding no legal work in Serbia, he went back to Greece and from there travelled through Bulgaria, Albania and Bosnia and across Italy to France, where he worked about four years and eight months and tried to regularise, but was caught before he got legal papers, though he had paid tax and completed the process, and was sent back to Bangladesh.
quotes: বৈধ কাজের সুযোগ না পেয়ে আবার গ্রিসে ফিরে আসি
ফ্রান্সে আমি প্রায় চার বছর আট মাস
drafts.why_new: A Greece-Bulgaria-Albania-Bosnia-Italy-France overland path, and deportation after nearly five years.

drafts.target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
drafts.claim: Sujan Mia of Chhatak, Sunamganj, deported from France, said on 18 April 2026 that when he then tried for an Australian visa a broker and an agency took BDT 17 lakh from him and gave him a fake visa.
quotes: দালাল ও এজেন্সি ১৭ লাখ টাকা নিয়ে
drafts.why_new: A deportee cheated again at home: BDT 17 lakh for a fake Australian visa.

drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > The contract price and the final price
drafts.claim: Mizanur Rahman of Phulsuti village, Nagarkanda, Faridpur, alleged at a human chain outside the Faridpur Deputy Commissioner's office on 14 October 2026 that a Faridpur trafficking ring, having promised to take him to Italy, held and tortured him in Libya and took BDT 60 lakh in three rounds.
quotes: তাঁকে ইতালি নেওয়ার কথা বলে
drafts.why_new: BDT 60 lakh in three rounds, the largest named single-victim total in the 2026 cases here.

drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > What happens
drafts.claim: Mizanur Rahman said that, still not released after the payments and seeing how severe the torture was, he broke a window, escaped and gave himself up to Libyan police, and later came home in 2026 through IOM; eleven people tortured by the same ring came home from Libya through IOM in 2026 and joined the human chain.
quotes: এরপরও মুক্তি না পেয়ে
চলতি বছর লিবিয়া থেকে অভিবাসন সংস্থার মাধ্যমে দেশে এসেছেন ১১ জন
drafts.why_new: A way out that worked: escaping and surrendering to Libyan police, then return through IOM.

drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > What happens
drafts.claim: At the same human chain, Taslima Begum said her husband Habib was killed because the family could not pay a ransom of BDT 10 lakh; she now lives with their three children at her father's house.
quotes: মুক্তিপণের ১০ লাখ টাকা দিতে না পারায়
drafts.why_new: A killing alleged over an unpaid BDT 10 lakh ransom.

drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > The law
drafts.claim: Asked about the returnees' demand for trial of the Faridpur ring, the Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Ops) of Faridpur said on 14 October 2026 that legal action would be taken if the victims' families complained, and that steps would follow investigation if anyone had filed a case; one victim at the human chain asked, 'Where do I go to get justice?'
quotes: ভুক্তভোগী পরিবারগুলো অভিযোগ দিলে
কোন জায়গায় গেলে বিচার পাব
drafts.why_new: Eleven returnees protesting publicly and the police still asking for a complaint: no case or arrest is reported.

drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > What happens
drafts.claim: According to investigators, on 5 August 2025 the wife of Md Saiful (39) of Sundarganj, Gaibandha, who had gone to Libya about two years before November 2026 through a Bangladeshi broker, got a call from a Libyan mobile number saying he was in the callers' custody, that BDT 30 lakh ransom must be paid or he would be killed, and that no one in the family would be allowed to speak to him until half the ransom was paid.
quotes: লিবিয়ার একটি মুঠোফোন নম্বর থেকে
৩০ লাখ টাকা মুক্তিপণ দিতে হবে
মুক্তিপণের অর্ধেক টাকা পরিশোধ না করা পর্যন্ত
drafts.why_new: A ransom demand with no proof of life: half must be paid before the family may hear the man's voice.

drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > What happens
drafts.claim: The CID said the family sent BDT 5 lakh in all between 10 and 25 August 2025 from a bKash shop at Bamandanga Hall Mor, Sundarganj, to several mobile numbers the accused gave, and that even after the money was received the family was not put in touch with Saiful.
quotes: একটি বিকাশের দোকান থেকে অভিযুক্ত ব্যক্তিদের দেওয়া একাধিক মুঠোফোন নম্বরে মোট পাঁচ লাখ টাকা পাঠান তাঁরা
কিন্তু টাকা পাওয়ার পরও
drafts.why_new: How ransom is paid inside Bangladesh: mobile-wallet transfers from a local agent shop to several numbers.

drafts.target_section: People who offer to get your money back
drafts.claim: According to the CID, after the family of a man held in Libya had paid BDT 5 lakh in August 2025, a man named Sohel contacted the hostage's wife, said he had all the information and would if necessary go to Libya himself to rescue him, and told her to come to the Kadamtali area of Dhaka; when she went there his phone was switched off.
quotes: এরপর সোহেল নামের এক ব্যক্তি
ঢাকার কদমতলী এলাকায় আসতে বলেন
drafts.why_new: A 'rescuer' approaching a hostage's family; extends the section from debt recovery to hostage recovery.

drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > What happens
drafts.claim: According to the CID, the father of the Gaibandha hostage was then contacted from another number and asked for a further BDT 42 lakh in the name of rescuing his son, and was told his son was held by two men in Libya named Mokarram and Anwar from whom the caller had got the father's number; the father said he would pay nothing more unless he could speak to his son directly, and no more calls came to him or to his son's wife.
quotes: আরও ৪২ লাখ টাকা মুক্তিপণ দাবি করা হয়
মোকাররম ও আনোয়ার নামের দুই ব্যক্তির কাছে
সরাসরি কথা বলিয়ে না দিলে
drafts.why_new: Successive callers demanding rising sums (30, then 42 lakh) with no proof of life; when the family insisted on speaking to him, the calls stopped.

drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > Where to get help
drafts.claim: The father of the Gaibandha hostage filed a case under the trafficking Act at Sundarganj police station on 5 September 2025, the case was sent to the CID for investigation, and on 12 November 2026 the CID arrested two men from Chandpur village, Singra, at Singra Bazar, Natore; the CID said it was still gathering information on where in Libya the son was held and on rescuing him.
quotes: গত বছরের ৫ সেপ্টেম্বর সুন্দরগঞ্জ থানায় মামলা করেন
গতকাল বৃহস্পতিবার দুপুরে নাটোরের সিংড়া বাজার
সাইফুলকে লিবিয়ায় কোথায় আটক রাখা হয়েছে
drafts.why_new: A second example of a family's police case reaching the CID and producing arrests, here 14 months after filing, with the hostage still not found.

drafts.target_section: Libya to Italy by boat > Where to get help
drafts.claim: In its statement on the Gaibandha case on 13 November 2026 the CID asked everyone to verify the legality of the person, the agency, the visa and the employing firm before going abroad.
quotes: সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তি, এজেন্সি, ভিসা ও নিয়োগকারী প্রতিষ্ঠানের বৈধতা যাচাই
drafts.why_new: The CID's stated advice (it does not say how to verify).

new_sections.heading: From the Gulf overland through Iran and Turkey to Greece
new_sections.why: Two accounts in this set (Faridul Alam, who left Dubai in 2010, article acc10e12; Sujan Mia of Chhatak, roundtable of 18 April 2026, article c9a1d235) describe the same route the guide does not cover: workers already in Dubai are taken by road to Oman, by boat to Bandar Abbas, across Iran and Turkey to Istanbul and by lorry into Greece, paying per border crossed. Suggested parts: How it is sold, The path, What happens. The detailed account dates from 2010-2014, so prices and border practice need a current source before the section is relied on.
